That's right, I'm using an acronym for the 'Dark Corners of Sensei's Library'. Everyone loves acronyms, right?

Today I have something to show you that will perhaps drive home just how massive Sensei's Library really is. Behold the Big Question Mark, a series of articles on SL where people submit questions about Go with the hopes that a strong player will come in and answer them. For example, question 401 is about a game between Chen Zude and Yang Yilun (quite possibly the most famous Go teacher in America). The article goes into some depth about why black resigned in this game.

The Big Question Mark has almost 600 entries. That is astonishing for a series of articles that most people (including Go players) aren't even aware exists. There's a lot of interesting stuff in there, so why not spend an afternoon avoiding all the rest of the insanity engulfing Voat and get lost in Go?
I swear these pumpkin seeds just germinated a few days ago. These things are monsters.

So...we always thought it would be great to put some pumpkins in a front garden, then when fall came, carve the pumpkins in place on the vine for Halloween. We bought a house with enough space a couple of years ago...so last year we put in three pumpkins along with some petunias.

Holy crap! Those pumpkins tried to take over the world! The vines were about 20 feet long before I started hacking them back. The poor petunias disappeared....even the bindweed couldn't compete.

We did end up with three massive pumpkins (lots of smaller ones didn't make it), but I will not try those again in a front garden.

I hope you have a nice big spot to let your big, monster babies run free!

I have this big spot at the front where there are a few bushes and nothing really else. It can expand as far as it wants until it looks unkempt. Yeah, you should really start pruning at about 10 ft. or the fruit can end up small/underdeveloped. It's also pretty easy to train the vines to grow in the direction you want them to.
